correctness.rationale: For an achiral perfect word, the start-index reflection is i -> C-i, C=c-k+1, and takes k-factors to reversed k-factors. Exactly q^ceil(k/2) palindromic factor types occur once in each residue modulo n; any fixed residue of the induced reflection lifts uniquely to a fixed position modulo L. Therefore q^ceil(k/2) f_n(C)<=f_L(C)<=2. Odd n implies q=2 and k=1 or 2; their constructions (01)^n and (0011)^n are perfect by gcd(step,n)=1 and achiral. Even n forces C odd because otherwise 2 fixed residues per palindrome would require >=4 fixed starts while the global reflection has only 2. Reversal pairs all remaining classes. The embedded independent finite enumerator tested 92,219 words across 14 parameter triples; these tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The 2016 foundational perfect-necklace full text gives reversal closure and the number of rotation necklaces, but no fixed-point classification. The known pure-reversal inequivalence for de Bruijn sequences only establishes the multiplicity-one binary subcase. The new palindromic-factor residue argument covers every odd multiplicity and alphabet, supplies the exact binary low-order exceptions and an even-multiplicity axis obstruction. Relevant published-finding corpus/own history searches show no covering claim; the residual risks below remain.
residual_risks: Older unindexed work on generalized perfect-necklace reversal fixed points or even-multiplicity astute graph symmetries could contain the odd-multiplicity result.
Full text of the general symmetric-bracelet paper was not examined; its published abstract states only unconstrained enumeration.
The known 1984 pure-reversal de Bruijn result was compared through the 2024 authorial exposition rather than a line-by-line reading of the original.

value.rationale: This settles the natural dihedral fixed-point question for the entire odd-multiplicity perfect-necklace family, over every finite alphabet. It gives the exact exceptional existence cases, converts a previously known rotation-class count to the complete bracelet count whenever odd multiplicity and the nonexceptional parameters apply, and identifies which reflection axes can occur at even multiplicity. Such a structural boundary is motivated by reversal ambiguity of universal cycles; it is not just a finite census or a re-expression of the already known necklace formula.
